approach: Add a records-derived hold; nothing is written. In scope_guard.rs, `RequestRecord` gets `verified_unlanded` (job verified but never closed: Blocked, or Dispatched with a passing verification, and no finished attempt). It is only a flag on the record; it never enters `attempts`, so T1 to T5 do not change. New `non_landed_attempts(requests, line, live)` counts the line's Rejected and Failed attempts through `group_lines`/`line_attempts`, plus each `verified_unlanded` request that a later request on the line has superseded (some other request has `retry_of` or `same_text_as` equal to its id) and that `live` does not report running. It ignores Environment attempts and counts 0 on a line with an Accepted attempt. New `hold_reason(requests, job_id, live)` returns a reason at 2 or more, and returns None for a job that is itself verified-and-unsuperseded (a pull request waiting to merge is not a retry candidate). In drain.rs a new default `Steps::awaiting(jobs)` (real impl: reap the registry, `request_records`, `hold_reason` with `self.athena.running`) is asked in `Drain::prepare` for jobs that are not paused, and merged into the held map with its cause carried to dependents, and at the top of each `Drain::attempts` iteration after the pause check (new `ItemEnd::Awaiting(reason)`, passed over). The hold is recomputed from committed records on every run.

decisions.choice: A verified-but-closed-less job counts as a non-landed attempt only once a later request on its line supersedes it (another request's `retry_of` or `same_text_as` names it), and never while `running()` reports it. A job that is itself verified and unsuperseded is never held.
decisions.reason: This answers finding 1. A pull request in `Landing::Waiting` stays Dispatched with a passing verification and no outcome (drain.rs:131-138, 1935; store.rs:57, 127-128). `interrupted_work` (steward.rs:447-480) lists it as an item, so `prepare` asks the hold about it. With nothing after it, it is the line's current candidate, not a failed retry, so it counts 0 and is not held. A queued 'try again on <job>' item is a request record whose `retry_of` names the earlier job (queued_work, steward.rs:402; `request_records` scope_guard.rs:631), so the collision case in criterion 2 still counts: c2 is superseded by the queued item. Liveness is passed as a closure like `interrupted_work` does with `running` (steward.rs:447), so it is unit-testable without the registry.

rejected.option: Count every Blocked or Dispatched+Pass job (previous plan)
rejected.why: Holds a line whose latest attempt passed and is waiting to merge (finding 1).

rejected.option: Guess from the drain's `passed.is_none()` check only
rejected.why: It covers the in-loop check but not `prepare`, which asks about every item including interrupted waiting ones.
scope_guard's request functions take records only; the registry lives on `Athena` (status.rs:2047). A closure keeps `hold_reason` pure.

decisions.choice: Count a line's attempts with new `scope_guard::non_landed_attempts` built on `group_lines` and `line_attempts`; expose `hold_reason` over `&[RequestRecord]` so drain tests can feed real `RequestRecord` values.
decisions.reason: The brief forbids a second line-grouping function. `Athena::line_pause`, `line_flag` and `live_marks` already group the same way. A pure function needs no git.

rejected.option: Count inside drain.rs from the run's `jobs` list
rejected.why: It does not see earlier runs and would be a second grouping.

rejected.option: Write a pause or flag file
rejected.why: That feeds `athena status` and `line_pause`, and its release is a named follow-up.

decisions.choice: Represent the verified-but-closed-less job as a bool on `RequestRecord`, not as an `AttemptRecord` or a new `Verdict` variant.
decisions.reason: `counted()` treats every verdict except Environment as an attempt for T1, T2 and T5, and T3 sums cost over attempts (scope_guard.rs:222-233, 237-243), so a variant or extra attempt would change T1 to T5, which is out of scope. `RequestRecord` literals exist only at scope_guard.rs:658 and in the `req()` test helper at 1789.

rejected.option: Make `verdict_of` return Failed for Blocked and open jobs
rejected.why: Same signal change, and turns a job awaiting `go` into a failure.

decisions.choice: Ask the hold in two places: `prepare` (beside `paused`, before any read) and the top of the `attempts` loop after the pause check (new `ItemEnd::Awaiting`). Not after the last failed attempt.
decisions.reason: The loop check stops the second attempt when one earlier failure plus the first attempt makes two, and stops a later drain run. `prepare` avoids paying a planning read for an unread 'try again on' item on a held line. A fresh item still gets both attempts, so existing Paused, Flagged and Failed ends keep their text.

rejected.why: An unread item on a held line would still be read in planning (prepare, drain.rs:2166).
The count changes during a run.

decisions.choice: Precedence and dependents: `paused` is asked first; `awaiting` is asked only for ids not paused. `prepare` keeps the cause of each held entry (a set `by_hold` of ids held by this rule) and copies it to dependents at every level of the dependents loop (drain.rs:2206-2223). Wording is 'its line is awaiting diagnosis' for hold-caused entries and the unchanged 'its line is paused' for paused-caused ones.
decisions.reason: Answers finding 2. The loop repeats, and a dependent of a dependent now inherits the cause of the entry it depends on, so no line is called paused when none is. With `by_hold` empty the text is byte-identical, so existing paused tests (tests/drain.rs:788, 835, 953, 1252, 1284) keep exact text. Reusing the `held` map reuses `pass_over_paused`, the `first_paused` filtering and the `athena plan` held listing.

rejected.option: A second map and printer for holds
rejected.why: Duplicates the held plumbing and risks double lines.

rejected.option: One wording that fits both causes
rejected.why: Would change existing exact-text assertions for paused dependents.

decisions.choice: Environment stops are never counted and a line with an Accepted attempt is never held. The reason text says 'awaiting diagnosis', names the line, the counts and that the drain will not retry it, and never says 'paused' or that a diagnosis job exists.
decisions.reason: Follows `counted()` and `done()` (scope_guard.rs:222-233) and the request. A real-steps test asserts no plan refusal contains 'paused' for a flagged line, and the pause text would send the operator to delete a pause file that does not exist.

rejected.why: Would hold lines for a full disk or an expired login.
Misleading; the follow-up work owns the release path.

decisions.choice: No request-text or reading rule is added or changed, so the refusal corpus gets no new case. The rule reads only job records. 'try again on <job>' is still parsed only by the existing `retried_job`.
decisions.reason: The refusal-corpus mapping applies to parsers and reading checks. This rule's input forms are record shapes, tabled in the tests: one Failed, two Failed, Rejected+Failed, Environment stops, Accepted in line, verified-superseded, verified-unsuperseded, live. `cargo test --locked` runs the corpus test, so any accidental effect shows.

rejected.why: The corpus tests request and reading text; nothing in the hold reads either.

risks.risk: A pull request waiting to merge, or a job landing now, is counted as a non-landed attempt and its line is held (finding 1).
risks.mitigation: A verified job without a closing record counts only once a later request on its line supersedes it, and never while `running()` reports it (checked through the `live` closure). A verified unsuperseded item is never held. Negative tests cover the waiting item, the liveness exclusion, and an item with two earlier failures plus its own waiting job.

risks.risk: If an operator asks 'try again on <waiting job>', that job is superseded and counts as one non-landed attempt, so a line [Failed, waiting, new retry] is held at the new retry.
risks.mitigation: Stated in the changelog bullet and the hold reason (it names the counts). The retry of a waiting job is an explicit request for a second attempt on a line that already failed once; holding it matches the rule. The release path is the named follow-up.

risks.risk: An existing real-steps or lifecycle test has a line that already reaches two counted attempts and then expects a retry, so it now fails.
risks.mitigation: The real-steps drains that retry use environment stops, interrupted jobs or fresh items, which are not counted or start at zero. The producer runs the full `cargo test --locked` and changes only a test whose expectation is that retry.

risks.risk: A held line has no release: it stays held until it lands or the request is rephrased.
risks.mitigation: This is the stated scope; the reason names the line and says the drain will not retry it. Nothing is written, so no cleanup is owed.

risks.risk: Adding a field to the public `RequestRecord` breaks other struct literals.
risks.mitigation: Searched all crates: literals exist only at scope_guard.rs:658 and in the `req()` helper at 1789. The compiler flags any other.

risks.risk: The hold at two attempts overlaps with the T1 flag at three and the T4 pause at two same-criterion rejections, so operators could see two reasons.
risks.mitigation: A pause is reported first and the hold is asked only for jobs not paused; the hold text says 'awaiting diagnosis', never 'paused'.

risks.risk: `RealSteps::awaiting` calls `registry().reap()`, which edits registry state as `queue()` does.
risks.mitigation: `queue()` already reaps before `running()` (drain.rs:4210); `awaiting` does the same for the same reason, so a dead process is not taken as live.

open_questions: User: There is no command to release a held line in this job (release is a named follow-up). Is it acceptable that the operator escapes a hold only by asking in new words, which starts a new line, until that follow-up exists?
